title: Can an LLM Repair a Language Model in Weight Space Without Gradient Training?
read_level: full main text (Secs 1-6, 8, 10-11) and appendix B-C manifest; Secs 7 and 9 (natural completion, induced failures) skimmed
why_wsp: An external tool-using LLM editor inspects a deliberately damaged Transformer (predictions, activation summaries, weight statistics) and selects projection recipes that the runtime applies to MLP/attention weights without gradient updates, compared against fixed and scripted selectors, black-box search, and LoRA.
domain: repair of injected low-rank faults in small LMs; adjective completion probe
editor: unnamed external LLM ('all editor model fields use a generic role identifier'; exact provider model revision not recorded)
interface: code/tensor tools (HTTP server tools: inspect, propose recipe, apply, dev-evaluate, revert, finalize; runtime performs the projection)
loop: closed-loop with feedback (up to five development evaluations; sessions used three or four)
self_editing: no; editor repairs separate small target models
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: Fixed recipe edits 64 columns in two MLP layers: "Position projection ... selects two anomalous layers, and removes a rank-one component on 64 estimated columns." (Sec 4.2); interface allows "a column budget up to 256" (Sec 3.2)

headline_results.claim: Pythia: live selection vs black-box vs fixed projection
headline_results.quote: For Pythia, live selection achieves 65.62% completion accuracy, compared with 0% for black-box search and 66.15% for a fixed projection.

headline_results.claim: Fixed projection matches live on core fault
headline_results.quote: these core cases show effective repair by both procedures, not a general live-controller advantage

headline_results.claim: Weight error after live editing (causal targets)
headline_results.quote: The three causal targets have final mean weight errors close to 0.068, 0.073, and 0.064.

headline_results.where: Table 1 (first candidate A / feedback A / Bayesian A / B / weight error)

headline_results.claim: Compound fault: LLM and scripted tie
headline_results.quote: The LLM-proposed programs identified the injected locations in all 15 model-seed cases and achieved a mean Test-A accuracy of 71.25 %

headline_results.claim: Scripted selector equal on compound fault
headline_results.quote: The scripted selector achieved the same values when evaluating the matched set of three candidates.

headline_results.claim: LoRA alone fails on Pythia; repair then LoRA works
headline_results.quote: On Pythia, ordinary LoRA remains at zero while live repair then LoRA reaches 71.35% at this training budget.
On BERT, ordinary LoRA reaches 97.40%, exceeding the 96.35% live-repair-plus-LoRA result.

cost.quote: The fifteen core sessions each use three; the five additional SmolLM2 sessions use three or four, for 63 development evaluations overall.

baselines_and_controls: Original and damaged checkpoints; oracle inverse (privileged); repetition penalty decoding; fixed position, dense, gated spectral, weight-SVD, rollout-diagnostic projections; context damping; scripted single/five-candidate, recipe selector, blended operator; random search and matched-budget Bayesian/UCB black-box (5 evals); LoRA, DoRA-, PiSSA-, LoReFT-style, support-masked LoRA, gradient-SVD init; repair-then-LoRA and projection-initialized LoRA.
runs_and_variance: "The primary live-versus-non-live comparisons used the same three fault seeds, 101, 202, and 303"; mean and sample SD reported; five seeds for non-live methods in appendix; paired Wilcoxon with Holm correction (Table 18); 20 recorded live sessions.
robustness_of_edits: Held-out Test B (syntax and distractor shift) for all methods; training from repaired weights (25/50/100 AdamW steps); boundary cases for training- and simulated-quantization-induced failures (Table 14, skimmed). Not tested on long-form outputs. | Added 2026-11-25 from PDF Sec 6.8, Table 9 (LoRA on the same task, three seeds): "On Pythia-70M, sequential repair-plus-LoRA rises from 55.73% at 25 steps to 83.33% at 50 and 84.38% at 100 steps (with Live-LLM repair-plus-LoRA rising from 71.35% to 80.21%), whereas standalone LoRA remains collapsed at 0.00% through 50 steps and reaches only 19.79% at 100 steps." This measures repair as an initialization for same-task LoRA, not retention of the edit under unrelated fine-tuning.
verification: Automated validation audit of saved aggregates: "It checks 15,725 saved aggregate fields and 1,920 binary item vectors ... with zero mismatches" (Sec 5.2); state-identifier checks. No formal verification.
memorization_vs_reasoning: Paper attributes gains to operator coverage and feedback-driven selection, noting 'the numerical projection is supplied by the environment' (Sec 10); 'A session's natural-language rationale is a record of its stated decisions and not an independent measurement of hidden reasoning' (Sec 3.4).
limitations_stated: Faults are localized and deliberately low rank, matched to the repair family; narrow adjective task; three or five fault seeds; first-vs-final comparison retrospective within sessions; information boundary is instruction-based, not enforced sandbox; editor model revisions and three conversations missing; adapter variants lack reference parity; Qwen non-live rows lack raw provenance.
cites_or_builds_on: Takehi et al. 2026 Sparks of Weight-Space Programming blog [1]
Hu et al. Exploring Weight-Space Programming [8]
notes_for_survey: Controlled repair study where the LLM only selects among environment-supplied projection operators; fixed and scripted selectors matched the LLM on most conditions, with feedback changing the outcome in recorded cases (e.g., one Qwen seed). Measures weight-space restoration error relative to the injected fault in addition to task recovery.
